To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prospective monitoring of DLCO, in combination with measurement serum SP-D and serum YKL-40, is useful to discriminate between everlomin-related ILD and alternative diagnoses, and that everolimus trough concentrations are not associated with everolimus-related interstital lung disease.

everolimus related respiratory problems occur in 56% of patients with advanced breast cancer, that a decline in DLCOc is predictive for everolimus discontinuance due to ILD, that serum YKL-40 and SP-D levels can be used to discriminate ILD and other diagnoses, that FDG-PET abnormalities do not predict the onset of ILD, and that there is no relationship between everolimus concentration in blood and the occurrence of ILD.

1) everolimus-related intersticial lung disease occurs frequently in breast cancer patients, 2) pulmonary function test with diffusion capacity of lungs for carbon mon oxide corrected for hemoglobin and serum biomarkers can help to discriminate intersticial lung diseases from other causes of lung symptoms, and 3) everolimus pharmacokinetices and FDG-Pet are of limited value for the prediction of intersticial lung disorders.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

everolimus-induced ILD is frequent in patients with advanced breast cancer and that prospective measurement of serum biomarkers (SP-D, YKL-40) and DLCOc are helpful to discriminate everolimus-induced lung disease from other causes of lung disease.
the combination of DLCOc, SP-D, and YKL- 40 is a promising tool to detect and predict everolimus-related interstial lung disease (ILD).
everolimus related ILD can be detected by a combination of pulmonary function tests and biomarkers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
everolimus is associated with a high incidence of respiratory signs and symptoms.
everolimus-induced interstitial lung disease occurs frequently, and is hard to discriminate from other causes of pulmonary problems.
